rejected.title: The trigonometric ratios
card: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is the longest side, across from the right angle. Pick one of the other angles. The opposite side faces that angle. The adjacent side is next to that angle and is not the hypotenuse.

tan = opposite ÷ adjacent. Example: sides 3, 4 and 5, with 3 opposite the angle and 4 adjacent. Then tan = 3/4 and sin = 3/5. Similar triangles give the same ratios for the same angle, even though their sides are different lengths.
rejected.remember: Label the sides from the angle you are using, then pick sin, cos or tan.

a.q: A right-angled triangle has sides 5, 12 and 13. For the angle that has 5 opposite and 12 adjacent, what is sin?
a.why: Sine is opposite ÷ hypotenuse. The hypotenuse is 13, so sin = 5/13. The ratio 5/12 is tempting, but that is tangent, which uses the adjacent side.
a.clue: Sine uses the opposite side and the longest side.

b.q: Triangle P has sides 3, 4 and 5. Angle A has 3 opposite and 4 adjacent. Triangle Q is similar, with the same angle A, and its hypotenuse is 15. What is the side opposite angle A in Q?
b.why: In P, sin A = 3/5. Q has the same angle, so sin A is also 3/5, and opposite ÷ 15 = 3/5 gives an opposite side of 9. Adding 10 to each side gives 13, but 13/15 is not 3/5, so that does not keep the ratio.
b.clue: The sine of angle A is the same in both triangles.

a.q: A right-angled triangle has sides 5, 12 and 13. For the angle that has 5 opposite and 12 adjacent, what is sin?
a.why: Sine is opposite ÷ hypotenuse. The hypotenuse is 13, so sin = 5/13. The ratio 5/12 is tempting, but that is tangent, which uses the adjacent side.

b.q: Triangle P has angle 40° with opposite side 4 and hypotenuse 6. Triangle Q is similar and bigger, with hypotenuse 18 at its 40° angle. What is the opposite side in Q?
b.why: The ratios are the same for the same angle, so sin 40° = 4/6 = 2/3 in both triangles. In Q, opposite ÷ 18 = 2/3, so the opposite side is 12. Adding the same amount to each side, which gives 10, does not keep the ratio.
b.clue: Similar triangles keep the same sine, so scale by the same multiple.

problems.detail: A triangle with opposite 4 and hypotenuse 6 has an angle of about 41.8°, not 40°, since sin 40° ≈ 0.643 while 4/6 ≈ 0.667. A student who checks on a calculator will find the data inconsistent. Use a different angle or different side lengths.
Why (b) says sin 40° = 4/6 = 2/3, which is false (sin 40° ≈ 0.643).
Why (b) says adding the same amount to each side gives 10, but going from hypotenuse 6 to 18 adds 12, so the opposite side would be 16, not 10. The explanation of the distractor is wrong.
'with hypotenuse 18 at its 40° angle' is awkward and unclear. Say 'its hypotenuse is 18' instead.
'the adjacent side touches it' is ambiguous, because the hypotenuse also touches the angle. It should say the adjacent side is the side next to the angle that is not the hypotenuse.

card: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is the longest side, across from the right angle. Pick one of the other angles. The opposite side faces that angle. The adjacent side is next to that angle and is not the hypotenuse.

a.q: A right-angled triangle has sides 5, 12 and 13. Angle B has the side 5 opposite it and the side 12 next to it. What is sin B?
a.why: Sine is opposite ÷ hypotenuse. The hypotenuse is 13, so sin B = 5/13. The ratio 5/12 is tempting, but that is tangent, which uses the adjacent side.
a.clue: Sine uses the opposite side and the longest side.

b.q: Triangle P has sides 8, 15 and 17, with 8 opposite angle A and 15 adjacent to it. Triangle Q has sides 16, 30 and 34 and the same angle A, with 16 opposite it. What is true about tan A?
opts: It is 8/15 in P and 16/15 in Q
It is twice as large in Q as in P
b.why: tan A = opposite ÷ adjacent. In P it is 8/15, and in Q it is 16/30, which is also 8/15. Similar triangles give the same ratios for the same angle, even though Q's sides are twice as long. 8/17 is sin A, not tan A, and 16/15 mixes a side from Q with a side from P.
b.clue: Work out opposite ÷ adjacent in each triangle and compare.

final.title: The trigonometric ratios
card: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is the longest side, across from the right angle. Pick one of the other angles. The opposite side faces that angle. The adjacent side is next to that angle and is not the hypotenuse.

\(\tan \theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}\). Example: sides 3, 4 and 5, with 3 opposite the angle \(\theta\) and 4 adjacent. Then \(\tan \theta = \frac{3}{4}\) and \(\sin \theta = \frac{3}{5}\). Similar triangles give the same ratios for the same angle, even though their sides are different lengths.
